´╗┐## User Story
As a user, I want to be able to change the application language in a settings menu so that I can use the app in my preferred native language (English, Spanish, Portuguese, French, or Hindi).

## Context
The application currently only supports English. To reach a global audience and provide an organic, personalized experience, we need to implement a robust i18n infrastructure that handles both static UI labels and future localized dynamic content from the backend.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **Auto-detection**: On first load, the app detects the system language using 
avigator.languages and sets it as active (if supported). Default is English.
- [ ] **Settings Screen**: A new screen for "Settings" accessible via a gear icon in the AppHeader or SideMenu.
- [ ] **Language Selector**: The settings screen includes a list of 5 languages (English, Spanish, Portuguese, French, Hindi) showing their native names and a flag icon (SVG-based).
- [ ] **Persistence**: The selected language is saved in localStorage and persists across sessions.
- [ ] **API Integration**: All outgoing requests from ^Gpi.ts include the Accept-Language header with the current language code.
- [ ] **UI Translation**: All static labels, buttons, and menu items are translated into the 5 base languages using i18next.
- [ ] **Lazy Loading**: Translation files are loaded on-demand from public/locales/ to keep the bundle size small.

## Technical Notes
- **Dependencies**: Add i18next, eact-i18next, i18next-browser-languagedetector, i18next-http-backend.
- **Icons**: Use a resilient SVG-based library for flags (e.g.,  lag-icons).
- **State Management**: Integrate i18next with the existing React context if needed, or use the useTranslation hook directly.
- **Routing**: Update App.tsx to include the settings screen in the manual router.
- **Files to create**:
    - src/app/i18n.ts (Configuration)
    - src/app/features/settings/SettingsScreen.tsx
    - public/locales/{en,es,pt,fr,hi}/translation.json
- **Files to modify**:
    - src/app/lib/api.ts (Add headers)
    - src/app/App.tsx (Add route)
    - src/app/components/AppLayout/SideMenu.tsx (Add navigation link)
    - package.json (Dependencies)

## Out of Scope
- Localizing existing mock recipe data (remains in original language for now).
- RTL (Right-to-Left) support for this iteration.
title: feat: implement internationalization (i18n) with settings menu

´╗┐## User Story

**As a** user browsing playlists,
**I want to** tap "Ver" on a playlist card and see all the recipes it contains,
**So that** I can evaluate a playlist's content before deciding to subscribe.

---

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Each playlist card in `BrowsePlaylistsScreen` has a "Ver" button
- [ ] Tapping "Ver" opens a new `PlaylistDetailScreen`
- [ ] The detail screen shows the playlist header: cover image, name, author, description, and key stats (recipe count, avg prep time, difficulty, rating)
- [ ] The detail screen lists all recipes in the playlist with: title, thumbnail, prep time, difficulty, and match percentage
- [ ] Each recipe in the list is tappable and navigates to `RecipeDetailScreen`
- [ ] A back button returns the user to `BrowsePlaylistsScreen`
- [ ] Loading and empty states are handled gracefully

---

## Technical Notes

- New screen: `PlaylistDetailScreen` inside `features/playlists/`
- New hook: `usePlaylistDetail(id)` using TanStack Query `useQuery`
- New service call: `getPlaylistDetail(id)` ÔåÆ `GET /playlists/{id}` (returns playlist + recipes)
- New types: `PlaylistItem` and `PlaylistDetail extends Playlist`
- Extend mock API client to handle `GET /playlists/{id}`
- Extend `Screen` union and `NavigateFn` in `App.tsx`
title: feat: view playlist contents from playlist card

## User Story

As a user, I want the system to suggest a recipe tailored to my stored taste profile and any preferences I can add on the spot, so that I can get instant, personalized inspiration when I don't know what to cook.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The screen shows a "Suggest a recipe" CTA that triggers the suggestion engine.
- [ ] Before or alongside the suggestion, the user can add one-time contextual preferences: available ingredients, mood/craving tags (e.g., "comfort food", "quick", "light"), and max prep time.
- [ ] One-time preferences do not overwrite the stored profile ÔÇö they apply only to the current request.
- [ ] The system returns a single recipe suggestion with a match explanation ("Based on your Keto preference and 'quick' tag").
- [ ] The user can accept the suggestion (navigate to recipe detail) or request a new suggestion.
- [ ] The user can save the suggested recipe to favorites directly from this screen.
- [ ] If no suitable recipe is found, a friendly empty state is shown with suggestions to relax filters.

## UX Notes

- Mobile-first layout (`max-w-md`).
- The suggestion reveal should feel like a moment of delight ÔÇö consider a card-flip or fade-in animation.
- Loading state must be explicit (skeleton or spinner with a short witty loading message).
- One-time preference chips should be easy to add and dismiss.

## Out of Scope

- Multi-recipe suggestion lists (single suggestion per request for MVP).
- Modifying the stored profile from this screen (that belongs in the onboarding/profile edit flow).
title: feat: AI Recipe Suggestion Screen

## User Story

As a user, I want to view and organize my favorite recipes, so that I can quickly find and revisit the recipes I love most.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The screen displays all recipes the user has marked as favorites (cover image, title, match percentage, difficulty, prep time).
- [ ] The user can search favorites by recipe name or ingredient.
- [ ] The user can filter favorites by: dietary regime, difficulty, and prep time range.
- [ ] The user can sort favorites by: date added (newest/oldest), match percentage, alphabetical, and prep time.
- [ ] The user can organize favorites into named folders (collections).
- [ ] The user can create, rename, and delete folders.
- [ ] The user can move a recipe from one folder to another.
- [ ] The user can remove a recipe from favorites directly from this screen.
- [ ] Empty state is shown when the user has no favorites, with a CTA to explore the feed.

## UX Notes

- Mobile-first layout (`max-w-md`).
- Folder view and flat list view toggle.
- Skeleton loaders while data is fetching.
- Swipe-to-reveal or long-press context menu for remove / move-to-folder actions.

## Out of Scope

- Sharing folders publicly.
- Collaborative folders.
title: feat: Favorite Recipes Screen

## User Story

As a user, I want to create my own recipe playlist by searching and adding recipes with filters and ordering, so that I can build personalized meal sequences tailored to my preferences.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The screen has a header section to set the playlist name, optional description, and cover image.
- [ ] A recipe search panel lets the user find recipes by: name, ingredient, tag, dietary regime, and difficulty.
- [ ] The user can sort search results by: match percentage, prep time, difficulty, and newest.
- [ ] The user can add a recipe to the playlist with a single tap.
- [ ] Added recipes appear in an ordered list below (or in a separate panel); the user can drag-to-reorder them.
- [ ] The user can remove a recipe from the playlist before saving.
- [ ] The playlist can be saved as private or public.
- [ ] The screen validates that the playlist has at least one recipe and a name before allowing save.
- [ ] On successful save, the user is navigated to the new playlist's detail screen.

## UX Notes

- Mobile-first layout (`max-w-md`).
- Two-panel layout (search + selected list) or tab-based navigation between "Search" and "My Playlist".
- Haptic feedback on recipe add/remove and reorder.

## Out of Scope

- Editing an already published playlist (separate screen/flow).
- Collaborative playlists.
title: feat: Create Custom Playlist Screen

## User Story

As a user, I want to see all the playlists I am subscribed to in one place, so that I can easily manage and navigate my curated meal sequences.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The screen lists all playlists the current user is subscribed to (cover image, title, recipe count, progress indicator).
- [ ] The user can filter the list by: dietary regime, difficulty, and completion status (in progress / not started / completed).
- [ ] The user can sort the list by: subscription date (newest/oldest), alphabetical, and match percentage.
- [ ] Tapping a playlist navigates to the playlist detail screen.
- [ ] The user can unsubscribe from a playlist directly from this screen (with a confirmation gesture/dialog).
- [ ] Empty state is shown when the user has no subscriptions, with a CTA to browse playlists.

## UX Notes

- Mobile-first layout (`max-w-md`).
- Skeleton loaders while data is fetching.
- Unsubscribe action should use a swipe-to-reveal gesture or long-press menu on mobile.

## Out of Scope

- Editing playlist contents.
- Creating new playlists from this screen.
title: feat: My Subscribed Playlists Screen

## Summary

Incorporates the anti-LLM-slop guidelines from Andrej Karpathy's post (Apr 2026) into our CLAUDE.md, based on the reference implementation at github.com/forrestchang/andrej-karpathy-skills.

## What's missing from main

The \main\ branch CLAUDE.md has no Behavioral Guidelines section at all. This PR adds it with improvements over the version on \ eature/ui-screens-design\.

## Changes

### New content (not in any branch)
- **Push back when warranted** ÔÇö explicitly added to \Think Before Coding\
- **Self-check heuristic** ÔÇö *'Would a senior engineer say this is overcomplicated?'*
- **200-lines-to-50 rule** ÔÇö rewrite before submitting if grossly over-scoped
- **Mention unrelated dead code, don't delete it** ÔÇö previously only implied
- **Litmus test** ÔÇö *Every changed line should trace directly to the user's request*
- **Goal plan template** ÔÇö \[Step] ÔåÆ verify: [check]\ format for multi-step tasks
- **Task transformation examples** ÔÇö concrete 'Add validation' ÔåÆ test-first equivalents
- **Strong vs weak success criteria** framing

### Carried over from \ eature/ui-screens-design\
- Full Behavioral Guidelines section (Think Before Coding, Simplicity First, Surgical Changes, Goal-Driven Execution, Project Workflow, Code Quality)
- Lab note #6 expanded with 3 failure iterations (PowerShell PATH + ExecutionPolicy + Bash vs PowerShell tool confusion)
- Lab note #8: \gh project item-add\ requires \project\ scope on gh token

## References
- Karpathy post: https://x.com/karpathy/status/2015883857489522876
- Reference CLAUDE.md: https://github.com/forrestchang/andrej-karpathy-skills/blob/main/CLAUDE.md
title: docs(claude): incorporate Karpathy behavioral guidelines into CLAUDE.md
